title: Runtime feature-flag contract and telemetry tethering (ADR)
author: Leah Gomez
summary: Defines a company-wide contract for runtime feature flags used by inference services, and requires explicit telemetry tethering so any behavioral change under a flag is observable, traceable, and rollable-back without service-level surprises.
body:
Overview:
This ADR standardizes how we introduce, operate, and retire runtime feature flags that affect API semantics, runtime execution (including model-serving switches), and infrastructure behavior. It pairs a lightweight contract for the flag lifecycle with mandatory telemetry tethering rules so that feature changes are always accompanied by structured observability and rollback controls.

Goals:
- Provide a predictable, safe pattern for enabling/disabling features at runtime across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Ensure every flag change produces sufficient telemetry to detect correctness regressions, latency/cost regressions, and SLO impacts.
- Minimize production blast radius and provide clear rollback and remediation steps.

Scope:
- Applies to any runtime toggle that changes: API response shape, model variant selection, quantization/precision modes, routing/failover behavior, billing/cost attribution flags, or scheduling priority hints.
- Out of scope: pure developer feature flags used only in local dev/test without live traffic, and compile-time build flags.

Flag contract (required fields):
Each runtime flag must be declared with the following canonical schema in the feature-flag registry (example JSON shown):

  {
    "flag_id": "string (kebab-case)",
    "owner": "team-name",
    "impact": "latency|cost|fidelity|security|availability|observability",
    "scope": "global|region:<region>|customer:<org-id>|route:<api-route>",
    "default_behavior": "on|off|safe-value",
    "rollout_window_minutes": "integer",
    "expiry_date": "YYYY-MM-DD or null (must be set for experiments)",
    "associated_observability_tags": ["string tags used in metrics/traces"],
    "rollback_playbook_link": "internal-link"
  }

Required semantics:
- Flag identifiers must be globally unique and kebab-case. Prefix experimental flags with "exp-".
- Owner must be a single team responsible for runbook, telemetry, and retirement.
- Impact must be at least one of the enumerated values; multi-impact flags list multiple types.
- Rollout windows default to 60 minutes unless waived by SRE with documented reasons.
- Flags that touch customer data or change privacy behavior require a "restricted" confidentiality tag and legal sign-off.

Telemetry tethering (mandatory):
Any rollout or state change for a flag must emit or be associated with the following telemetry artifacts:
1) A control-plane event with: flag_id, actor_id, previous_state, new_state, rollout_scope, timestamp.
2) A trace/annotation on requests that observe altered behavior. For high-volume routes where per-request annotation is expensive, sample at 1% and attach a deterministic sample id keyed by request-hash.
3) Metric slices: for each impacted SLI, provide metric labels containing the flag_id and the rollout cohort (e.g., "flag=exp-model-quantize-2025;cohort=canary").
4) Synthetic probes: automated synthetic checks must run against the altered path during the rollout window with explicit success/failure criteria.

Observability requirements:
- SLIs to monitor when toggling flags: request_p50_ms, request_p95_ms, request_p99_ms, error_rate, cost_per_1000_tokens, model_quality_regression_score (where available).
- Alerting: create a rollout alert that fires if any SLI deviates beyond the defined threshold in the flag's declaration (default thresholds: +15% p95 latency, +10% error rate, +5% model quality delta).
- Dashboards: every flag change automatically generates a temporary dashboard with time-series comparing cohorts (control vs flag) anchored to change time. Dashboards must persist at least 7 days.

Performance and overhead budget:
- Synchronous flag checks must complete in <1ms p99 in the serving hot path. If a flag check risks exceeding 2ms p99, it must be cached locally with a TTL no longer than the flag's rollout_window_minutes and be designed to accept eventual consistency.
- Maximum allowable CPU/latency overhead introduced by flag evaluation is 2% of p95 tail for the affected route; exceedance requires pre-approval by Performance Standards owner.

Runtime distribution and infra rules:
- We use signed feature bundles for private/onprem deployments. Bundles are versioned and applied via the private runtime sidecar with a Kafka-backed change stream for Hosted.
- Flag change propagation SLO: 95% of nodes must apply non-rollback flag changes within 30s, 99% within 2 minutes.
- If a deployment cannot meet propagation SLOs, rollout must proceed with smaller cohorts and stricter synthetic checks.

Model-serving specifics:
- Flags that switch model variants (e.g., quantized vs float, beta model versions) must declare a "quality watermark": a minimum acceptable model evaluation score against the current prompt-suite. If the flagged variant fails the watermark in the synthetic probes, automated rollback occurs.
- KV cache compatibility: model-switch flags must respect cache keying semantics. If cache key format changes, a cache-warmup and backwards-compatibility shim is required.

Safe rollout procedure (step-by-step):
1) Register flag in the registry and attach rollback_playbook and associated_observability_tags.
2) Create synthetic probes and a temporary dashboard; configure alerts and define acceptance criteria.
3) Start with cohort=10% (randomized by request hash) for 60 minutes.
4) Evaluate SLI deltas and synthetic probe results. If stable, escalate to 50% for 2 hours.
5) Full rollout to 100% only after passing a manual checkpoint and sign-off from the flag owner and SRE.
6) If any alert triggers or synthetic probes fail, execute rollback_playbook immediately and open an incident.

Rollback playbook (example checklist):
- Abort any further rollout steps and set flag to previous_state in registry.
- Trigger automated rollback on the control-plane and confirm bundle reversion on >95% of nodes.
- Capture forensic telemetry: collect traces, sampled payloads, and model output diffs for 5 minutes before/after the rollback point.
- Notify stakeholders via the incident channel tagged with the flag_id and include the temporary dashboard link.

Coding/Library guidance:
- Use the central feature flag client library (ff-client) that provides: typed flag retrieval, local TTL caching, IDEMPOTENT evaluation, and telemetry annotation helpers.
- Example usage (pseudo-code):

  // Acquire flag with safe default
  flag = ff.getFlag('exp-llm-quantize-2025', default=false)
  if (flag.isEnabled(request)) {
    trace.annotate('flag.exp-llm-quantize-2025','cohort=canary')
    model = modelSelector.select('quantized-v2')
  }

- Avoid scattering boolean checks across codebase; encapsulate flag behavior behind a single function in the owning service to simplify rollback.

Security and compliance notes:
- Flags toggling data retention, telemetry sampling, or PII handling must be reviewed by Security & Privacy and flagged as "restricted".
- Flag bundles delivered to Private/on-prem customers must be signed with the platform's release key and include a manifest with SHA256 checksums.

Decision rationale:
We adopt a combined contract+telemetry approach rather than a permissive flag model to reduce blind rollouts and hard-to-debug regressions. Attaching telemetry labels and synthetic probes by default makes regressions observable early and automates safe rollback for critical model-serving experiments.

Consequences and trade-offs:
- Pros: Faster, safer rollouts; better auditability; reduced mean time to detect regressions.
- Cons: Slight increase in platform complexity and modest telemetry/alerting costs. Teams will need to invest time to write synthetic probes and define quality watermarks for model variants.

Operational runbook (short):
- On alert: escalate to flag owner + SRE, pause rollouts, run rollback checklist.
- Post-incident: produce a short incident review that includes telemetry anchored to flag rollout and propose a mitigation (e.g., lower cohort, change default).
- Retirement: flags must be removed from code and registry within 90 days of finalization or after expiry_date if set.

Implementation timeline and next steps:
- Q3 2025: Ship ff-client 1.0 with TTL cache, annotation helper, and registry integration.
- Q4 2025: Enforce registry validation in CI for all PRs that introduce runtime flags.
- Q1 2026: Integrate automatic dashboard generation and synthetic probe templates in Console.

References and artifacts:
- ff-client API docs: internal link to library README
- Synthetic probe templates: internal link to monitoring repo
- Example rollback playbook: internal link to runbooks

Appendix: example registry table (recommended fields):
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| flag_id | unique kebab-case id | exp-llm-quantize-2025 |
| owner | owning team | eng-serving-runtime |
| impact | main impact class | fidelity,cost |
| scope | rollout scope | route:/v1/generate |
| default_behavior | safe default | off |
| rollout_window_minutes | default window | 60 |
| expiry_date | soft expiry for experiments | 2025-08-31 |
| associated_observability_tags | labels used for metrics/traces | ["flag=exp-llm-quantize-2025"]
decision: Adopt a strict feature-flag contract coupled with mandatory telemetry tethering and synthetic probes for any runtime toggles that touch the inference serving path. Use a central client library and signed bundles for distribution to Private deployments.
consequences: Improved detection and rollback speed for model-serving and API changes at modest cost in observability and rollout engineering. Requires teams to author probes and adhere to registry schema; SRE will enforce propagation SLOs and may require smaller cohorts in constrained environments.
rollout_plan: Deliver ff-client primitives in Q3 2025, add CI registry validation by Q4 2025, and Console integration for dashboards/synthetic probe templates by Q1 2026. Early adopters: 3 serving teams for pilot in Q3.
ops_runbook: Pause rollouts on alert, revert flag state, confirm bundle propagation, collect traces and model diffs, notify stakeholders, create incident review. Retirement: remove code paths and registry entry within 90 days of stabilization.
compliance_impact: Flags that change telemetry or PII handling require Legal/Security review and must be marked restricted. Signed bundles and manifest checks are required for Private/on-prem customers.
